value.body: A museum or curatorial assistant helps look after a collection: recording each object, checking its condition, and helping put together exhibitions. Employers include museums, private galleries, heritage trusts, university collections and cultural NGOs. A typical day mixes documentation work, handling objects with care, and helping with visitors, events or research requests.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: BA in Anthropology, History, Archaeology or Fine Arts

items.label: Often helpful
items.value: A diploma or master's in museology

items.label: Museums set up by the Ministry of Culture (cumulative)
items.note: Includes ~145 opened in the nine years to 2023; counts only Ministry-established museums, not every museum in India
items.source: Ministry of Culture, Directory of Museums in India (as reported)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually begin through internships, project-based documentation work or short contracts at museums and heritage organisations. A postgraduate diploma or master's in museology is commonly asked for in permanent positions.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Careful handling and storage of artefacts

value.title: At a glance
items: Permanent openings are limited; contract and project roles are common.
Anthropology adds an understanding of material culture and communities behind objects.
Next roles: curator, collections manager, education officer.
